music:
Create a NEW flat 2D scientific mechanism figure for ForeDance on white, panoramic 3.2:1. The visual style must be strictly front-facing flat vector editorial graphics: solid colors, fine outlines, no perspective, no tilted surfaces, no depth, no 3D, no extrusion, no shadows, no glow, no glass, no gradients. Visually engaging through colored feature mosaics, a circular zoom inset and curved connectors, not a uniform box flowchart. Use teal #009EAC music, blue #0769F9 structure, orange #FF8A17 residual, purple #8534DB mask/state, navy text. Helvetica, very sparse labels. No title, explanation cards, full equations, paragraphs, or table.
Preserve this overall left-to-right composition. Left 60%: a tiny flat music-feature icon goes through a simple 2D funnel labeled “Project + time” with a clock outline. It feeds a horizontal TEAL feature mosaic of small cells, labeled “Forecast · 25 Hz”. Under this on the SAME time axis place a thin BLUE line of query dots, labeled “Motion · 15 Hz”. A flat circular magnifier centered over the right part of both rails enlarges two forecast neighbors and ONE intervening motion-time query. Two fine teal strokes converge at that query, label “Interpolate”. No individual tick labels or claimed exact sample counts. A short downward arrow from the query yields a small flat teal feature strip ĉ_i. The entire feature mosaic and all cells remain uncurved, upright, and orthographic.
Right 40%: aligned ĉ_i splits into two flowing but FLAT teal bands ending at side-input ports of two small modulation nodes labeled “FiLM”. The top main activation path contains two small blue flat layer bars, label “Structure”; bottom has two orange bars, label “Residual”. Each activation exits its backbone bars, then splits into a local modulation path and a skip path rejoining at a plus circle. The aligned teal music enters only the MODULATION side port. A small purple binary on/off staircase m_i gates the modulation branch, not the skip. The output top is blue token squares; bottom orange residual bars. Small orange flame silhouette beside each trainable modulator, no glow. Do NOT show separate decoded humanoids, skeletons, or robot outputs. No teal input to backbone beginning.
Make this feel crafted, airy and compact, with a strong asymmetrical silhouette and clear negative space. Color variation comes from mosaic cells, flat curved bands, circle lens and small layer bars. No 3D effects anywhere. Keep all labels short and remove prose footers.
representation:
Create a NEW flat 2D scientific diagram for ForeDance codec training, panoramic 3.2:1 on white. Strict orthographic vector artwork: solid fills, crisp outlines, no perspective, no tilted planes, no shaded spheres, no extrusion, no shadows, no gradients, no glow. Visually rich through a point lattice, residual vector, curved gradient arcs and small coordinate-coverage strips. Avoid conventional rows of large boxes. No overall title, no paragraphs, no note cards, no table. Sparse Helvetica and mathematical italics. Blue structure, orange residual, purple state, teal input, navy text.
LEFT 20%: four thin front-facing motion-feature strips x, drawn as tiny abstract line/dot traces, enter a FLAT encoder wedge Eφ with a small orange flame. Output z enters the main latent inset.
CENTER 35%: an upright, flat 2D latent-space diagram, no perspective or depth. An irregular softly outlined pale-blue region contains a sparse grid of identical solid BLUE prototype dots. One selected prototype e(q) is a larger blue circle. Encoder point z is a black dot nearby. A straight ORANGE vector r connects e(q) exactly to z. These are schematic latent coordinates, not experimental data. Label only e(q), r, z and “Latent space”. Main emphasis is the discrete point plus continuous offset.
RIGHT 45%: a black curved arrow from z to the upper flat decoder wedge Dψ, labeled “Full”; a BLUE curved arrow from e(q) to the lower identical wedge Dψ, labeled “Structure”. Small orange flame silhouettes on both wedges. A short thin dashed vertical link between them says “shared”. A single flat PURPLE pose-and-velocity glyph b, with no arrow on the pose itself, feeds both decoder side ports through separate unobstructed purple arcs. No wire runs through a decoder to reach the other.
The two outputs are small front-facing feature strips x̂_f and x̂_s and losses L_f/L_s. Four compact coverage rows to the far right labeled x, ẋ, p, ṗ. EVERY cell in the upper full-view grid is colored blue or orange. EVERY lower structural-view row contains some blue selected cells plus empty outlined cells, including both p rows. These swatches represent coordinate selection, not measurement. No explanatory table labels.
Show two thin reverse-gradient arcs in separate open lanes: ORANGE from upper decoder input back to z labeled ∇r, BLUE from lower decoder input back to z labeled ST. Do not place a stop-gradient barrier across the blue forward path. A tiny key “ST: straight-through” can sit at the lower margin. Keep the two principal reconstruction paths, source z/e(q), and shared b clear. No third path or anatomical picture. All geometry is flat 2D.
commit:
Create a NEW strictly FLAT 2D scientific mechanism illustration for ForeDance Commit Forcing, panoramic 3.2:1 on pure white. Solid vector colors, thin outlines, no perspective, no tilted plane, no spheres, no 3D, no shadow, no glow, no gradient. Blue structure, orange residual, purple context, teal recorded targets, navy ink. Make the composition visually interesting with two aligned time ribbons, a compact selection switch, and a 2D vector construction. Sparse Helvetica plus clear math. No big title, paragraphs, explanation cards, table or repeated multi-box pipeline.
LEFT 43%: two thin horizontal context ribbons stacked, labeled “TF” and “CoF”. In EACH row history is represented by TWO rows of blue/orange tiles; tiny row labels D and C. A bracket spanning BOTH tile rows is labeled h* for TF, h̃ for CoF. A thin PURPLE vertical divider separates this history from a flat purple posture-plus-velocity-trace glyph labeled b* or b̃. The pose glyph itself has no directional arrow. Do NOT label the orange residual row as b. Both history and boundary are fields of one paired context.
A small blue/orange committed pair below the CoF ribbon branches jointly to its history and boundary under a bracket “joint update”. Small sg on this construction arrow. The TF and CoF pairs go through a small selection switch into one FLAT purple training wedge “Learn” with a crisp orange flame.
RIGHT 57%: a FRONT-FACING 2D geometric target construction. A simple thin horizontal axis and vertical axis frame the points, no numeric ticks or slanted projection. One fixed TEAL circle z* sits upper-right and is labeled “Recorded target”. One blue point e(q*) sits lower-right; another blue point e(q̂) sits lower-left. A faint but flat orange dashed vector r* from e(q*) ends exactly at z*. A stronger solid orange vector r*rebased from e(q̂) ends at that SAME z*. Label “Rebase” briefly along the stronger vector. The shared endpoint makes latent target preservation visually explicit. Learner output q̂ connects to the e(q̂) anchor. Do not connect generated boundary to z*.
Above the learner, a small fixed blue target token q* goes straight into a blue loss circle L_q; a separate predicted-logits wire from Learn also enters L_q. Near the solid rebased residual vector, a tiny orange L_r marks residual supervision; connect it to the rebased vector, not from z* alone. Keep loss routes distinct from the two geometric arrows. No sentence explaining the identity at the bottom; the accompanying paper caption handles it. No large legend. Crisp compact vector illustration, all surfaces flat and upright.
